context: The value to delete is 4. The initial tree contains values 3 through 15 and has root 8. The table lists all initial connections. “Empty” means there is no child. The pointer cur always refers to the object that originally held 4.

Steps 1 and 2 leave the connections unchanged. Step 3 detaches the original node 5. Only in step 4 is the value 5 written into cur. Except for the changes specified at each step, the table's connections stay the same. The right subtree rooted at 12 stays intact throughout. The successor pointer nex in the figure corresponds to tmp in the code.
description: The figure follows the code: recursively delete the successor first, then overwrite the value of cur. If cur were changed to 5 first, a search from the root to delete the value 5 would hit cur first. The two steps in this code cannot simply be swapped.

frames.announcement: Locate the target node cur, which holds 4 and has two children.
frames.explanation: The target value 4 is less than root 8, so go left to find cur (currently 4). Its left child is 3 and its right child is 6. Node 6 has left leaf 5 and right leaf 7, as shown in “Connections throughout the tree before deletion.” Since cur has degree 2, we cannot simply cut its parent edge. Here we use the minimum value in its right subtree as a replacement.
frames.key_state: The node cur is to the left of root 8 and holds 4. It has left child 3 and right child 6. Node 6 has left child 5 and right child 7. Nothing has changed yet.
frames.title: Locate the target with two children

frames.announcement: Find the smallest node in the right subtree of cur, node 5, and mark it as the inorder successor nex.
frames.explanation: Follow cur (4) → 6 → 5 to the inorder successor and point nex to the original node 5. Root 8 still has left child cur, cur has left child 3 and right child 6, and 6 has left child 5 and right child 7. No value or connection has changed. As the minimum in the right subtree, 5 is larger than 3 on the left and smaller than the remaining values 6 and 7 on the right, so the replacement preserves the search ordering.
frames.key_state: The value of cur is still 4. Its left child is 3 and its right child is 6. The pointer nex points to 6's left leaf, 5, and 6 has right child 7. Nothing has changed yet.
frames.title: Find the inorder successor, 5

frames.announcement: First detach the original successor leaf 5 from the left of 6. At this stage cur still holds 4.
frames.explanation: Recursively delete leaf 5, referenced by nex, by clearing 6.left. Root 8 has left child cur (still holding 4). The left and right children of cur are 3 and 6. Node 6 has no left child and has right leaf 7. Only the original node 5 has been detached. All other connections still match the initial table. The pointer nex retains a reference to the original node so its value can be read in the next step. The dashed circle marks its old position for comparison. It is no longer a node in the tree.
frames.key_state: The original node 5 has been detached. The value of cur is still 4, with left child 3 and right child 6. Node 6 has no left child and has right child 7.
frames.title: Detach the original successor node

frames.announcement: Overwrite the original value 4 in cur with the successor's value 5 to finish deleting a node with two children.
frames.explanation: Write the successor's value 5 into cur, overwriting 4. Root 8 has left child cur (now holding 5), and cur has left child 3 and right child 6. Node 6 has no left child and has right leaf 7. Only the value of cur has changed. Its links to parent 8 and children 3 and 6 stay the same. The original node 5 has been detached, leaving exactly one value 5 in the tree.
frames.key_state: The value of cur is now 5, with left child 3 and right child 6. Node 6 has no left child and has right child 7. The original node 5 is detached, and deletion is complete.
frames.title: Write the successor's value into cur

result: When deletion is complete, the tree no longer contains the value 4. The cur object remains in place, and the other nodes and the search ordering are preserved.
summary: To delete a node of degree 2, first locate and detach its inorder successor in the right subtree. Then write the successor's value into the target node cur.

tables.caption: Connections throughout the tree before deletion

title: Deleting a node with two children from a binary search tree
